records.issue_text: showingLast never becomes true on the real last page when member count is an exact multiple of limit, because totalPages is inflated
records.rationale: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, which over-counts by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50 → totalPages=3 though only 2 pages exist). showingLast (propertyEqual of currentPage and totalPages) then never triggers on the actual last page, so 'next' stays enabled; conversely 'next' can advance offset to user_count (Math.min in the next action) yielding an empty page. A Math.ceil computation is required.

records.issue_text: totalPages computed property in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing an off-by-one extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50 yields 3 pages instead of 2) — should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), causing spurious server requests for empty pages
records.rationale: The diff shows `totalPages: function() { ... return Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1; }`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50), floor(2)+1 = 3 instead of the correct 2, so showingLast is false at the real last page and `next` advances offset to user_count (Math.min(offset+limit, user_count)), fetching an empty page. This is a verifiable off-by-one defect introduced by the new pagination code.

records.issue_text: Unbounded `limit` parameter in groups_controller.rb members action allows any signed-in user to request limit=100000000 (or negative limit, which PostgreSQL treats as no limit), forcing the server to load and serialize the entire group membership, causing memory/CPU exhaustion and an easy DoS vector — needs a server-side clamp
records.rationale: The diff adds `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` in groups_controller.rb#members with no clamping. A negative or zero limit in PostgreSQL/ARel means no LIMIT clause, and a huge limit loads/serializes the whole membership table. Unlike the previous code, this endpoint now publicly exposes pagination params for all groups (not just automatic ones), making the unbounded parameter directly exploitable. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.
